verdict.rationale: The only first-party evidence touching this story is the dbt Projects on Snowflake doc, which says users can 'develop, deploy, orchestrate, and observe' transformations on managed dbt runtimes. That implies some workflow orchestration, but it never explicitly mentions recurring schedules. Snowpipe (event-driven loading), streams (change tracking) and dynamic tables (only a release-note title) are adjacent features or building blocks, not documented scheduling, so they earn no credit. Missing for 10: an explicitly documented scheduler for recurring jobs (cron or interval triggers), DAG or multi-step workflow scheduling beyond dbt, programmatic/API control of schedules, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
